---
title: "Trimes"
---

trimes (transient time series) is a python package for transient time series data in pandas format. The application is actually for all time series data where the time vector has a numerical format (e.g numpy's float64) - as opposed to the frequently used *DateTime* format. To the best of our knowledge, there is currently no other python package focusing on transient time series data as described and the mentioned  *DateTime* format is not convenient for transient time series.

trimes provides functionality for pandas DataFrames (in the format mentioned above) for the following use cases:

- get data points
- interpolation
- resampling
- regression
- signal generation (harmonics, symmetrical components)
- comparison of times series (difference, boundaries, envelopes)
- metrics (e.g. root mean squared error)
- step response analysis
- plotting
- FFT / spectra (`trimes.fft`) and a single-tone frequency / amplitude / phase estimator (`trimes.phasor`)
- analytic test signals with closed-form ground truth (`trimes.analytic`), the IEC/IEEE 60255-118-1:2018 test matrix and TVE / FE / RFE compliance metrics (`trimes.synchrophasor`), for benchmarking phasor / frequency / ROCOF estimators

and more.

Most of these helpers are also available as methods on a Series or DataFrame
through the `.trimes` accessor, e.g. `df.trimes.resample(1e-3)` or
`s.trimes.between(0.1, 0.3)` (see the [getting started tutorial](tutorials/getting_started.qmd)).

Have a look at the [tutorials](tutorials/overview.qmd) to get started.

## Installation

```
pip install trimes
```

The core -- `import trimes`, the `.trimes` accessor, `trimes.base`,
`trimes.analytic`, `trimes.phasor` and `trimes.synchrophasor` (its `plot`
submodule aside) -- needs only numpy and pandas. Heavier functionality is
behind optional extras:

| extra | pulls in | enables |
|-------|----------|---------|
| `trimes[viz]` | matplotlib | `trimes.plots`, `PeriodicSignal.plot*` |
| `trimes[dsp]` | scipy | `trimes.fft`, `.filter`, `.derivative`, `signal_processing.get_angle` |
| `trimes[control]` | python-control, icecream | `trimes.control` (step-response info) |
| `trimes[all]` | all of the above | everything |

```
pip install "trimes[all]"
```

Every submodule is reachable as an attribute after a bare `import trimes`
(e.g. `trimes.fft.rfft`), imported lazily so the optional dependencies are only
pulled in when you actually use that submodule.
